body: Most likely we're not apply `ecmaFeatures` for inline environments correctly. As a workaround, you can try adding `env: { es6: true }` to your config file.
Facing the same issue. It's not optimal to have it in the config file in an ES5 and ES6 mixed environment.
You can toggle it on and off in different config files `es6: true` in one and `es6: false` in another.

If I use 2 different config files, won't I have to duplicate all the configs, and they'll get out of sync?

I use the extension `.es6` for my ES6 files. May be there could be config option to enable certain options for certain file extensions? May be I'm thinking too far.

Ok, I started working on this (I think it's actually an easy fix), but run into a bunch of things that I can't test and explain. Here's the code that currently applies inline environments: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/eslint.js#L306
From what I can tell, that code is broken and currently doesn't do anything at all for rules (verified) as it tries to merge in `true` value into existing object.
This is the only code I can find that deals with `eslint-env` comment. However, somehow, global variables are being set correctly when enabling environments that way. I can't find that code anywhere.
I also don't see any way to verify that after I set `eslint-env` rules will be enabled in config and ecmaFeatures will get copied. eslint doesn't expose any of those options unfortunately. So I don't think it's possible to unittest my fix.

issue.body:
I've got a project all written in ES6, except for a single file that is in ES5.

In my .eslintrc:

``` yaml
env:
  es6: true
  node: true
  browser: true
```

In the single ES5 file:

``` js
/*eslint-env es6:false*/

const fn = () => {};
```

I expected to get an eslint error for the fat arrow, but there's no error.

issue.body:
I use ESLint extensively both at work and in my personal projects. If the projects are big and old, then sometime it ends up being a mix of ES5 and ES6 code as we're gradually transitioning to ES6 over time. It's not possible to enable ES6 transpilation for everything at once as some libraries/files won't work with strict mode enabled (which is automatically enabled by babel in strict mode).

The approach I've followed is to enable transpilation for only files with extension `.es6` and `.jsx`. But since there is no way to enable/disable es6 environment (#2705, #2614, #2604, #2134), sometimes it's always possible to write ES6 code in a file with ".js" extension, hence breaking the code.

Also, there are rules like `jsx`, which only make sense for `jsx` files. I shouldn't be able to write `jsx` in a file which is not transpiled.

Hence it would be great to configure `ESLlint` to enable/disable environments/rules according to the file extension.

One approach could be to have a base rules file, and ability to specify additional rule files/rules.

e.g.- 

```
{
    "extensions": {
        ".jsx": { "ecmaFeatures": { "jsx": true } },
        ".es6": ".eslintrc-es6"
    }
}
```
